what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to give symbolic support to the Marshall Park master plan as presented by the Parks Commission.
The board said the Finance Committee may use town counsel on a bylaw to amend the capital plan, if it brings a draft; members said they oppose the bylaw on the merits.
The chair is to relay that the board is unanimously opposed to the capital-plan proposal on its merits at this time.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of a conservation commission administrative assistant, a position created in the fiscal 23 budget.
The board signed the FY22 end-of-year transfer form, and tabled the Unitil streetlight purchase and license agreement to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The Marshall Park vote carries no funding, and the board heard that the next phase, the septic repair and the way the park would be paid for (grants, taxes or fundraising) are all unresolved, so a later request for money could reach Town Meeting.
A bylaw letting the capital plan be amended from the floor would change how Town Meeting voters can alter capital spending, and the board has said it opposes it as it stands.
watch_next: The late-August board meeting on town finances and ARPA, before requests are invited.
The next meeting's agenda: the Ritter building window denial and the tabled Unitil streetlight agreement.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main votes, the $2,190.28 transfer and its components, and the decisions on Finance Committee counsel use, Chestnut Street and the Unitil tabling. Our figures are mostly caption-garbled. The one thing to know: the official minutes record a 4-1-abstention warrant vote that ours lacks, and they have no record of the board's Conservation-bylaw opposition message or the late-August ARPA meeting.
